extracted.intended_audience: general readers; math enthusiasts; math communicators and educational video producers
extracted.subtask_description: Conventions and production features of Numberphile videos and its related podcast(s): interview-driven short-form math videos that aim to make mathematical concepts accessible to non-specialist viewers, plus a longer-form podcast series. Useful as a narrow exemplar for producing/populating a popular-math YouTube channel and companion podcast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video format — interviewer with expert
rubrics_metrics.description: Most videos consist of Haran interviewing an expert on a number, mathematical theorem or other mathematical concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a conversational interview structure led by a host (Brady Haran) with a guest expert; emphasize explanation through dialogue rather than lecture. Examples on the page: episodes featuring experts discussing numbers, theorems, or concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation style — brown paper drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The expert usually draws out their explanation on a large piece of brown paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor simple, hand-drawn visuals (large brown paper) to illustrate ideas step-by-step. This tactile sketching is a consistent stylistic device on the channel to make abstract ideas concrete for viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience accessibility — understandable to non-mathematicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Videos ... attempt to make the concepts understandable to the average, non-mathematician viewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize clear, non-technical language, intuitive examples, and visual aids to reach a general audience rather than specialist mathematicians. Avoid excessive jargon or proofs without motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content focus — from specific numbers to advanced concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: In the early days of the channel, each video focused on a specific number, but the channel has since expanded its scope, featuring videos on more advanced mathematical concepts such as Fermat's Last Theorem, the Riemann hypothesis and Kruskal's tree theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Episodes may be narrowly focused (a single number) or broadened to explain deep/advanced topics; choose topic scope according to intended audience accessibility and episode length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest selection — use of university professors and communicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Videos on the channel feature several university professors, maths communicators and famous mathematicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invite credible subject-matter experts (academics, well-known communicators) to lend authority and varied perspectives; guests often both explain and draw examples live.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary channel — Numberphile2 for extra detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Haran also runs the 'Numberphile2' channel, which includes extra footage and further detail than the main channel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a secondary channel or platform for extended cuts, deeper dives, behind-the-scenes material, or additional technical detail that would be too long or specialist for the main channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Podcast format — interview genre and runtime
rubrics_metrics.description: The Numberphile Podcast — Genre: Interview; Length: 25–75 minutes. Haran started a podcast titled The Numberphile Podcast in 2018 as a sister project. The podcast focuses more heavily on the lives and personalities of the subjects of the videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For longer-form audio content, adopt an interview style emphasizing personal stories and context; plan episodes within roughly 25–75 minutes to match the stated format. Use the podcast to explore biographical and human-interest angles complementary to the short videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production partnerships/support
rubrics_metrics.description: It is supported by the Mathematical Sciences Research Institute (MSRI) and Math for America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnering with reputable institutions or sponsors can provide credibility, resources, and potential access to experts; acknowledge and leverage institutional support in promotion or content.
